dinners.name: Thai Chicken Salad with Chilli Lime Dressing
dinners.description: A vibrant, crunchy salad with poached chicken, shredded cabbage, carrots, herbs, and crispy noodles, dressed in a zesty chilli lime dressing with the classic Thai sweet-sour-salty-spicy balance. Substantial enough for a full dinner.
dinners.why: Monday salad night — hearty enough for dinner with protein, kid-friendly crunch, and a dressing Elsie can handle (mild heat). No cooking the main protein separately; poach chicken in advance.

dinners.name: Chicken Broccoli Stir Fry
dinners.description: Restaurant-quality stir fry with tender chicken and bright green broccoli florets in a savory sauce of soy, oyster sauce, and sesame oil. Broccoli gets steamed first for perfect texture, then everything comes together in 5 minutes on the stove.
dinners.why: Uses up the fresh broccoli, comes together in under 20 minutes active time, kid-approved flavors. Perfect quick weeknight meal for solo dad — serve over rice.

dinners.name: One Pot Shrimp & Andouille Jambalaya
dinners.description: A hearty Louisiana classic with smoky andouille sausage, juicy shrimp, and chicken thighs simmered with the Cajun holy trinity (celery, onion, bell pepper), crushed tomatoes, and long-grain rice. Bold, warming, and deeply satisfying — everything cooks in one pot.
dinners.why: From the family 'want to make' list! One pot = easy cleanup for solo dad. Can be made milder for Elsie by reducing cayenne. Shrimp goes in at the end so it stays tender.

dinners.name: Honey Garlic Salmon with Steamed Broccoli
dinners.description: Pan-seared salmon fillets glazed with a caramelized honey-garlic sauce made from just four pantry ingredients: honey, soy sauce, garlic, and vinegar. The sauce turns golden and sticky in the pan. Served alongside steamed broccoli for a complete, beautiful meal.
dinners.why: Total time under 20 minutes — the ultimate solo-dad dinner. Uses up fresh broccoli as the side. Elsie loves honey glazes, and the salmon looks impressive for minimal effort.

dinners.name: Chicken Shawarma Pitas
dinners.description: Bite-sized chicken thigh pieces marinated in a fragrant blend of cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, and cayenne, then baked on a sheet pan until charred and juicy. Served in warm pita pockets with tahini sauce, arugula, and fresh tomato-cucumber salad.
dinners.why: Satisfies the house rule for Middle Eastern cuisine. Can marinate ahead, bake in 30 min. Build-your-own pitas are interactive and fun for Elsie. Warm spices without heat.

dinners.name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
dinners.description: Tender chicken pieces in a rich, creamy tomato-butter sauce spiced with garam masala, cumin, turmeric, and chili. A chef recipe that delivers restaurant-quality flavor with supermarket ingredients. The yogurt marinade makes the chicken incredibly tender.
dinners.why: Saturday celebration dinner when Laura returns — impressive but approachable. Elsie loves the mild, creamy sauce. Serve with rice and naan for a feast. Can prep the marinade Friday night.

dinners.name: Korean Beef Bulgogi Bowl
dinners.description: Thinly sliced beef marinated in a uniquely Korean blend of soy sauce, grated apple, grated onion, sesame oil, and garlic, then stir-fried until caramelized. The apple adds subtle sweetness and helps tenderize the meat. Served over steamed rice with quick-pickled veggies.
dinners.why: Quick stir-fry format (15 min cook time). Grated apple in the marinade is a revelation kids love — sweet-savory without any heat. All supermarket ingredients.

dinners.name: Broccoli Cheddar Soup with Crusty Bread
dinners.description: A rich, creamy, and ultra-cheesy broccoli soup built on a butter-flour roux with sharp cheddar stirred in low and slow. Better than Panera's version — loaded with tender broccoli florets and julienned carrots. Vegetarian comfort food at its finest.
dinners.why: Vegetarian option that uses up fresh broccoli. A drizzly Wednesday night comfort bowl. Elsie loves broccoli cheese soup. Make a big batch — leftovers reheat beautifully for lunch.

dinners.name: Peanut Noodles with Tofu and Vegetables
dinners.description: Chewy udon noodles tossed in a creamy, spicy peanut sauce made from peanut butter, tamari, sesame oil, fresh ginger, rice vinegar, and lime juice. Topped with julienned carrots, cucumber, tofu, and a shower of fresh herbs and crushed peanuts.
dinners.why: Vegetarian, kid-approved (what kid doesn't love peanut butter noodles?), and ready in under 30 minutes with zero cooking except boiling noodles. Can be served cold — perfect make-ahead for a rehearsal night.

dinners.name: Baked Falafel Pitas with Tahini Sauce
dinners.description: Crispy-outside, tender-inside falafel made from soaked dried chickpeas, fresh herbs (parsley, dill, cilantro), and warm spices, baked on a sheet pan instead of fried. Served in warm pita with tahini sauce, pickled onions, and a simple tomato-cucumber salad.
dinners.why: Vegetarian option with Middle Eastern flair. Lighter than fried. Requires soaking chickpeas overnight, so plan a day ahead. Build-your-own pita assembly is interactive for Elsie.

appetizers.name: Baba Ganoush with Warm Pita
appetizers.description: Smoky, creamy eggplant dip with tahini, garlic, lemon juice, and a touch of Greek yogurt for extra richness. Charred over an open flame for authentic smokiness, then blended smooth and drizzled with olive oil and toasted pine nuts.
appetizers.why: Pairs beautifully with the shawarma or falafel nights. Can be made 2-3 days ahead. The smokiness is irresistible and Elsie loves dipping things.

appetizers.name: Whipped Feta Dip with Fig Marsala Sauce
appetizers.description: Silky whipped feta and cream cheese dip, topped with a decadent sauce of dried Mission figs poached in Marsala wine, scattered with chopped pistachios and fresh mint. Comes together in 10 minutes and looks like a million bucks.
appetizers.why: A showstopper appetizer for Saturday when Laura returns. Sweet figs + salty feta is a flavor combination that wows. 10-minute prep makes it effortless.

salads.name: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad with Lemon-Herb Dressing
salads.description: An artfully arranged platter of tender chickpeas, halved grape tomatoes, crisp cucumber, briny Kalamata olives, and pickled red onions, showered with fresh parsley, dill, and mint. Substantial enough for a standalone dinner with crusty bread.
salads.dressing: Bright lemon vinaigrette: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 small garlic clove (minced), 1/2 tsp kosher salt, freshly cracked black pepper. Whisk together at the bottom of a large bowl before adding ingredients.
salads.flavor_rationale: The acid from lemon and brine from olives cut through the starchy richness of chickpeas. Fresh herbs add aromatic brightness, while pickled onions provide a tangy, sweet counterpoint. This is the Mediterranean principle of balancing earthy legumes with sharp, bright flavors — fat (olive oil) + acid (lemon) + salt (olives) + sweet (pickled onion) in every bite.
salads.seasonal_note: Early March on the East Coast: greenhouse herbs, stored garlic, and pantry chickpeas are at their best. Hothouse cucumbers and early grape tomatoes are available and improving in quality as spring approaches.
salads.why: Composed dinner salad — substantial enough for Monday salad night. Vegan, packed with protein from chickpeas. Arrange components in sections for visual impact.

salads.name: Thai Chicken Salad with Chilli Lime Dressing
salads.description: A generously portioned tossed salad with poached and shredded chicken, crunchy shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, fresh mint, cilantro, and crispy fried shallots, all tossed in a tangy-sweet chilli lime dressing with fish sauce depth.
salads.dressing: Thai chilli lime dressing: 2 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp chilli garlic sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp vegetable oil. Whisk until sugar dissolves. Adjust lime/fish sauce to taste for the signature sweet-sour-salty-spicy balance.
salads.flavor_rationale: The four pillars of Thai flavor — sweet (sugar), sour (lime), salty (fish sauce), and spicy (chilli) — create an electrifying dressing that wakes up raw vegetables. Crunchy cabbage and carrots provide textural contrast to tender chicken, while fresh herbs add aromatic complexity. The peanuts bring fat and crunch, rounding out every bite.
salads.seasonal_note: Cabbage, carrots, and fresh herbs are widely available in early March. This salad doesn't rely on peak-season produce, making it ideal for early spring.
salads.why: Tossed dinner salad — hearty enough for a full meal. The dressing is mild enough for Elsie (1 chilli rating on the site's scale). Can poach chicken ahead for fast assembly.

salads.name: Broccoli Salad with Smoky Tamari Almonds
salads.description: Crisp raw broccoli florets and diced stems tossed in a tangy, lightly creamy dressing with dried cranberries and sharp red onion, topped with smoked paprika-tamari roasted almonds and pepitas for irresistible crunch.
salads.dressing: Tangy mustard dressing: 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 2 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp honey, salt and pepper. Whisk until emulsified. The smoky tamari nut topping: toss almonds and pepitas with 1 tbsp tamari, 1/2 tsp maple syrup, 1/4 tsp smoked paprika; toast at 350°F for 12 min.
salads.flavor_rationale: Raw broccoli's bitter, vegetal crunch is tamed by the sweet-tart cranberries and the honey in the dressing. The mayo-vinegar dressing is lighter than classic broccoli salad but still coats thoroughly. Smoky tamari nuts replace bacon with a vegetarian umami bomb — same salty-smoky satisfaction without the meat.
salads.seasonal_note: Broccoli is excellent in early spring on the East Coast — sturdy, affordable, and at its sweetest. This salad improves over 2-3 days in the fridge, making it a perfect prep-ahead side.
salads.why: Uses up the fresh broccoli supply. Make-ahead side that pairs with almost any dinner this week. Gets better over days — ideal for a busy tech-week schedule.

salads.name: Fattoush Salad with Sumac-Lemon Vinaigrette
salads.description: A vibrant Lebanese bread salad with crispy toasted pita shards, crunchy romaine, juicy tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, and fresh herbs (parsley and mint), tossed in a tangy lemon-sumac vinaigrette with a touch of pomegranate molasses.
salads.dressing: Sumac-lemon vinaigrette: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp sumac, 1 tsp pomegranate molasses (optional), 1 small garlic clove (minced), salt and pepper. Whisk together and drizzle over salad just before serving to keep pita crispy.
salads.flavor_rationale: Sumac's fruity, citrusy tang is fattoush's defining flavor — it bridges the earthy pita and bright vegetables. Pomegranate molasses adds a sweet-tart depth that elevates a simple salad to something extraordinary. The contrast between crispy pita and cool, juicy vegetables is texturally addictive. This is the Middle Eastern mastery of acid + crunch + herb.
salads.seasonal_note: Romaine and radishes are solid early-spring choices on the East Coast. Sumac and pomegranate molasses are pantry staples that bring warm-weather brightness to transitional March produce.
salads.why: Pairs perfectly with shawarma, falafel, or any Middle Eastern dinner this week. The crispy pita makes it fun for Elsie. Quick assembly if pita is toasted ahead.

beverages.name: New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc (Marlborough)
beverages.description: A crisp, aromatic white wine with bright notes of citrus, passion fruit, and cut grass. The zippy acidity and mineral finish pair exceptionally with seafood, making it a natural match for the jambalaya's shrimp and the honey garlic salmon.
beverages.why: The high acid cuts through rich, buttery salmon glaze and stands up to Cajun spice. Look for Cloudy Bay, Kim Crawford, or Oyster Bay — widely available at $12-18.
beverages.pairing_note: Best with: Honey Garlic Salmon, Shrimp Jambalaya. The bright acidity cleans the palate between bites of rich, glazed fish or spicy rice.

beverages.name: Belgian-Style Witbier (Blue Moon or Allagash White)
beverages.description: A hazy, refreshing wheat beer brewed with coriander and orange peel. The light citrus and spice notes complement Middle Eastern flavors beautifully, while the soft body won't overpower lighter dishes.
beverages.why: The coriander and citrus in the beer echo the warm spices in shawarma and falafel. A crowd-pleasing, easy-drinking beer for a warm spring evening.
beverages.pairing_note: Best with: Chicken Shawarma, Baked Falafel, Thai Chicken Salad. The wheat body and citrus notes bridge Middle Eastern and Thai spice profiles.

beverages.name: Sparkling Mint Lemonade (Limonana)
beverages.description: A refreshing Middle Eastern iced lemonade blended with fresh mint leaves and topped with sparkling water. The combination of bright citrus and cool mint is incredibly thirst-quenching — a staple across the Levant and a family-friendly drink everyone can enjoy.
beverages.why: Elsie-approved! A fun, fancy-feeling drink for the whole family. Especially refreshing with the warm 70°F+ weekend forecast. Make a big pitcher for Saturday's celebration dinner.
beverages.pairing_note: Best with: Any dinner this week, especially Middle Eastern dishes. The mint and lemon echo the herbs and citrus in shawarma, falafel, and fattoush.
